title: Onion and Potato Soup
ingredients: 1 cup shredded old Cheddar cheese (250 mL)
directions: In a large Dutch oven, add onions and butter and saute for 5 minutes, or until onions are tender.
Add potatoes and broth. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 15 minutes.
Remove from heat and puree soup in a blender or food processor until smooth.
Return hot soup to Dutch oven and add milk, cheese and celery seed. Gently reheat until cheese melts. Do not boil.
Makes 6 - 8 servings.
notes: The celery seed adds an unusual but tasty flavour to this soup.

title: Hearty Alberta Chowder
ingredients: 1 lb. (500 g) Chorizo, Italian or your favourite fresh Pork sausage
12 fl oz (341 ml) kernel corn, undrained
5 cups (1.25 l) beef broth and water*
1/4 tsp. (1 ml) each thyme, salt and pepper
directions: *2 (10 fl oz/284 ml) cans beef broth with 2 cans water makes 5 cups/1.25 ml.
1. In a large heavy saucepan, saute Pork sausage over medium heat 10 to 11 minutes, until sausage browned; remove from pan; drain; slice thinly and keep warm.

2. Heat oil in soup pot; add onion, garlic, celery and green pepper; stir and cook 4 minutes or until vegetables are softened. Stir in flour; cook 1 minute. Add potatoes, carrots, corn and liquid, broth, tomatoes, 1 cup (250 ml) water, Worcestershire sauce, bay leaves, thyme, salt and pepper; bring to a boil; cover and simmer 6 minutes.
3. Add cooked sausage and continue cooking until vegetables are tender, about 6 minutes. Sprinkle with parsley.

title: Country Beef Ragout
ingredients: 2 (2) large celery stalks, cut in 1" (2.5 cm) pieces
1 (1) can (28 oz/796 ml) whole seasoned tomatoes
1 tsp. (5 ml) concentrated liquid beef stock (i.e. Bovril)
directions: 1. Brown beef cubes on all sides in lightly oiled skillet. Remove and place in oven-proof casserole.

2. In the skillet, cook onions, garlic and celery for 2 - 3 minutes and stir in remaining ingredients, except mushrooms. Bring to boil, stirring constantly. Season with salt and pepper and pour over beef.

3. Cover casserole and place in preheated 350°F (180°C) oven. After 1 hour, add mushrooms and cook for another 1-1/2 hours, removing lid for last 15 minutes. Serve over noodles or garlic mashed potatoes.

Time Saver Tip: To make this stew in a hurry, mix 1 pouch (approx. 56 g) quick stew mix with water according to package directions. Add beef and marinate in pot for 30 minutes. Bring to a boil, add remaining ingredients (using a 14 oz/398 ml) can of tomatoes instead) and simmer covered for 20 - 30 minutes.
notes: This delicious stew can also be made in the slow cooker, just combine all ingredients and cook covered for 5 - 6 hours on High, or 10 - 12 hours on Low.
Preparation time: 15 minutes. Cooking time: 2-1/2 hours. Makes 4 servings.
One serving: 249 Calories; 29 g Protein; 8.7 g Fat; 14 g Carbohydrates
Reprinted with permission from the Beef Information Centre. For more recipes visit www.beefinfo.org

title: Beatrice Stuffed Mushrooms
ingredients: 1 cup chopped stems and pieces from domestic mushrooms
3 tablespoons softened cream cheese or sour cream
1/4 cup fine, dry bread crumbs, seasoned with pinch of salt and pepper
directions: 1. Clean the mushroom caps with a brush.
2. Sauté the bacon with the shallots until the bacon fat liquefies.
3. Pour off most of the bacon fat, and replace with a little of the melted butter.
4. Mix in the chopped stems and pieces, cream cheese or sour cream, bread crumbs, parsley, and salt and pepper.
5. Place the cleaned mushrooms, stem side up, on a buttered broiler pan, and fill with the mixture, heaping into rounds.
6. Drizzle a little melted butter on them, and broil until heated through and lightly browned, about 1 to 2 minutes.
LOW CALORIE RECIPE: For a lighter filling use Beatrice Light Cream Cheese and Yogurt in place of Beatrice Regular Cream Cheese and Sour Cream.
notes: Printed promotional sheet headed HERITAGE with mushroom drawings; section header FIRST COURSES
Low calorie variation given
raw_text:
HERITAGE
BEATRICE STUFFED MUSHROOMS
12 fairly large domestic mushroom caps
2 strips bacon, chopped
1 tablespoon shallots, chopped fine
2 tablespoons melted butter
1 cup chopped stems and pieces from domestic mushrooms
3 tablespoons softened cream cheese or sour cream
1/4 cup fine, dry bread crumbs, seasoned with pinch of salt and pepper
1/4 teaspoon chopped parsley
Salt and pepper to taste
FIRST COURSES
1. Clean the mushroom caps with a brush.
2. Sauté the bacon with the shallots until the bacon fat liquefies.
3. Pour off most of the bacon fat, and replace with a little of the melted butter.
4. Mix in the chopped stems and pieces, cream cheese or sour cream, bread crumbs, parsley, and salt and pepper.
5. Place the cleaned mushrooms, stem side up, on a buttered broiler pan, and fill with the mixture, heaping into rounds.
6. Drizzle a little melted butter on them, and broil until heated through and lightly browned, about 1 to 2 minutes.
LOW CALORIE RECIPE
For a lighter filling use Beatrice Light Cream Cheese and Yogurt in place of Beatrice Regular Cream Cheese and Sour Cream.

title: Colcannon
directions: Boil potatoes in water until tender. Drain and set potatoes aside.
In a pan, add cabbage, green onions and 1/4 cup (50 mL) water. Bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover and simmer for 5 minutes or until cabbage is tender crisp.
Meanwhile, mash potatoes and add in milk, butter, salt and pepper. Beat until potatoes are fluffy. Stir in cabbage mixture. Serve hot.
Makes 6 servings.
notes: Potatoes play an essential part in the Irish diet.
